question: How many students are in the database?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students;

question: How many departments exist?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM departments;

question: List the names of all departments.
expected_sql: SELECT name FROM departments;

question: Find the student with student_id 1.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM students WHERE student_id = 1;

question: How many students have the last name 'Smith'?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students WHERE last_name = 'Smith';

question: Find the course with code 'CS101' if it exists, otherwise any 100 level course.
expected_sql: SELECT name FROM courses WHERE course_code = 'CS101' OR course_code LIKE '%100%';

question: How many instructors are there?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM instructors;

question: List all instructors with the title 'Professor'.
expected_sql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM instructors WHERE title = 'Professor';

question: Find instructors hired after 2010.
expected_sql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM instructors WHERE hire_year > 2010;

question: List all courses that are worth 4 credits.
expected_sql: SELECT name FROM courses WHERE credits = 4;

question: What is the total sum of all scholarship amounts awarded?
expected_sql: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM scholarships;

question: What is the average attendance percentage across all records?
expected_sql: SELECT AVG(attendance_percentage) FROM attendance;

question: What is the maximum score achieved in any assessment?
expected_sql: SELECT MAX(score) FROM marks;

question: What is the minimum score achieved in any assessment?
expected_sql: SELECT MIN(score) FROM marks;

question: Find the email of the student with student_id 5.
expected_sql: SELECT email FROM student_profiles WHERE student_id = 5;

question: List student first names and their department names.
expected_sql: SELECT s.first_name, d.name FROM students s JOIN departments d ON s.department_id = d.department_id;

question: List course names and their department names.
expected_sql: SELECT c.name, d.name FROM courses c JOIN departments d ON c.department_id = d.department_id;

question: Count the number of students in each department.
expected_sql: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) FROM students GROUP BY department_id;

question: What is the average score for each assessment name?
expected_sql: SELECT assessment_name, AVG(score) FROM marks GROUP BY assessment_name;

question: What is the total scholarship amount per student?
expected_sql: SELECT student_id, SUM(amount) FROM scholarships GROUP BY student_id;

question: List instructors and their department names.
expected_sql: SELECT i.first_name, i.last_name, d.name FROM instructors i JOIN departments d ON i.department_id = d.department_id;

question: Count the number of courses offered by each department.
expected_sql: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) FROM courses GROUP BY department_id;

question: List all students born after 2000, ordered by their date of birth.
expected_sql: SELECT first_name, last_name, date_of_birth FROM students WHERE date_of_birth > '2000-12-31' ORDER BY date_of_birth;

question: Count the number of enrollments for each status.
expected_sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM enrollments GROUP BY status;

question: Find department IDs that have more than 100 students.
expected_sql: SELECT department_id FROM students GROUP BY department_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 100;

question: Find the average course credits per department.
expected_sql: SELECT department_id, AVG(credits) FROM courses GROUP BY department_id;

question: List instructors hired before 2005, ordered by hire year descending.
expected_sql: SELECT first_name, last_name, hire_year FROM instructors WHERE hire_year < 2005 ORDER BY hire_year DESC;

question: Find courses with more than 3 credits in the 'Computer Science' department.
expected_sql: SELECT c.name FROM courses c JOIN departments d ON c.department_id = d.department_id WHERE c.credits > 3 AND d.name = 'Computer Science';

question: List students who enrolled in the year 2021.
expected_sql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM students WHERE enrollment_year = 2021;

question: Find the student ID with the highest single scholarship amount.
expected_sql: SELECT student_id FROM scholarships ORDER BY amount DESC LIMIT 1;

question: List all course names a student with ID 10 has enrolled in.
expected_sql: SELECT c.name FROM courses c JOIN course_offerings co ON c.course_id = co.course_id JOIN enrollments e ON co.offering_id = e.offering_id WHERE e.student_id = 10;

question: What is the average score for each course across all its offerings?
expected_sql: SELECT c.name, AVG(m.score) FROM courses c JOIN course_offerings co ON c.course_id = co.course_id JOIN enrollments e ON co.offering_id = e.offering_id JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id GROUP BY c.course_id, c.name;

question: Which departments have an average student assessment score greater than 70?
expected_sql: SELECT d.name FROM departments d JOIN students s ON d.department_id = s.department_id JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id GROUP BY d.department_id, d.name HAVING AVG(m.score) > 70;

question: Find all students who have dropped at least one course.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT s.first_name, s.last_name FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id WHERE e.status = 'Dropped';

question: Find instructors teaching more than 2 offerings in 2023.
expected_sql: SELECT i.first_name, i.last_name FROM instructors i JOIN course_offerings co ON i.instructor_id = co.instructor_id WHERE co.academic_year = 2023 GROUP BY i.instructor_id, i.first_name, i.last_name HAVING COUNT(*) > 2;

question: Find students who do not have any scholarships.
expected_sql: SELECT s.student_id FROM students s LEFT JOIN scholarships sc ON s.student_id = sc.student_id WHERE sc.scholarship_id IS NULL;

question: List the top 5 students with the highest average score.
expected_sql: SELECT e.student_id, AVG(m.score) as avg_score FROM enrollments e JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id GROUP BY e.student_id ORDER BY avg_score DESC LIMIT 5;

question: Find course offerings with a capacity greater than 100 that have more than 50 enrollments.
expected_sql: SELECT co.offering_id FROM course_offerings co JOIN enrollments e ON co.offering_id = e.offering_id WHERE co.capacity > 100 GROUP BY co.offering_id HAVING COUNT(e.enrollment_id) > 50;

question: What is the average attendance percentage per department?
expected_sql: SELECT d.name, AVG(a.attendance_percentage) FROM departments d JOIN students s ON d.department_id = s.department_id JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id JOIN attendance a ON e.enrollment_id = a.enrollment_id GROUP BY d.department_id, d.name;

question: Find students taking courses in more than 1 department.
expected_sql: SELECT s.student_id FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id JOIN course_offerings co ON e.offering_id = co.offering_id JOIN courses c ON co.course_id = c.course_id GROUP BY s.student_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.department_id) > 1;

question: Find instructors who have taught in both Fall and Spring semesters.
expected_sql: SELECT instructor_id FROM course_offerings WHERE semester = 'Fall' INTERSECT SELECT instructor_id FROM course_offerings WHERE semester = 'Spring';

question: List courses that have never been offered.
expected_sql: SELECT course_id FROM courses WHERE course_id NOT IN (SELECT course_id FROM course_offerings);

question: Which department's students have received the highest total scholarship amount?
expected_sql: SELECT d.name FROM departments d JOIN students s ON d.department_id = s.department_id JOIN scholarships sc ON s.student_id = sc.student_id GROUP BY d.department_id, d.name ORDER BY SUM(sc.amount) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: What is the most popular course by total historical enrollments?
expected_sql: SELECT c.name FROM courses c JOIN course_offerings co ON c.course_id = co.course_id JOIN enrollments e ON co.offering_id = e.offering_id GROUP BY c.course_id, c.name ORDER BY COUNT(e.enrollment_id) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: What is the average score of students with scholarships?
expected_sql: SELECT AVG(m.score) FROM marks m JOIN enrollments e ON m.enrollment_id = e.enrollment_id JOIN students s ON e.student_id = s.student_id WHERE s.student_id IN (SELECT student_id FROM scholarships);

question: Rank students by their overall average score.
expected_sql: SELECT student_id, AVG(score) as avg_score, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY AVG(score) DESC) as rank FROM enrollments e JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id GROUP BY student_id;

question: Find the instructor whose students have the highest average score.
expected_sql: SELECT i.instructor_id, i.first_name, i.last_name FROM instructors i JOIN course_offerings co ON i.instructor_id = co.instructor_id JOIN enrollments e ON co.offering_id = e.offering_id JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id GROUP BY i.instructor_id, i.first_name, i.last_name ORDER BY AVG(m.score) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: What percentage of students in each department have dropped at least one course?
expected_sql: WITH DroppedStudents AS (SELECT DISTINCT student_id FROM enrollments WHERE status = 'Dropped'), DeptTotals AS (SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) as total_students FROM students GROUP BY department_id), DeptDropped AS (SELECT s.department_id, COUNT(ds.student_id) as dropped_students FROM students s JOIN DroppedStudents ds ON s.student_id = ds.student_id GROUP BY s.department_id) SELECT dt.department_id, IFNULL(dd.dropped_students * 100.0 / dt.total_students, 0) as drop_percentage FROM DeptTotals dt LEFT JOIN DeptDropped dd ON dt.department_id = dd.department_id;

question: Find the student who has taken the highest number of unique courses.
expected_sql: SELECT e.student_id FROM enrollments e JOIN course_offerings co ON e.offering_id = co.offering_id GROUP BY e.student_id ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT co.course_id) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: Calculate the year-over-year difference in total course enrollments.
expected_sql: WITH YearlyEnrollments AS (SELECT co.academic_year, COUNT(e.enrollment_id) as total_enrollments FROM course_offerings co JOIN enrollments e ON co.offering_id = e.offering_id GROUP BY co.academic_year) SELECT academic_year, total_enrollments, total_enrollments - LAG(total_enrollments) OVER (ORDER BY academic_year) as yoy_difference FROM YearlyEnrollments;
